newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan shares rise slightly at end of weekly trade.
newsitem.headline: Jordan shares rise slightly at end of weekly trade.

text.p: Jordanian shares finished a touch higher at end of weekly trade on Wednesday with signs of market fatigue after a recent rebound, dealers said.
The Amman Financial Market 60-share index rose 0.07 percent to 149.59 points, hovering in a tight range since mid-last week, as shares worth 700,397 dinars ($ million) changed hands.
Brokers said the market appeared to be running out of steam with activity reverting back to buying by floor traders as institutional investors stay on the sidelines.
Speculative trade on select stock by institutional players that underpinned prices appears to have petered out, dealers said.
Star performer, Livestock and Poultry, which has dominated trade all week, continued to be focus of investor activity.

But a fall of 0.03 dinar to 0.90 dinar on turnover worth 329,592 dinars depressed sentiment. It had doubled in price in recent weeks, prompting board members to start sell their shares to cash in on the rise.
Some demand on select industrials accounted for the bulk of remaining trade, with some activity on Jordan Cement Factories that pushed the stock up a minimal 0.10 dinars to 3.340 dinars.
Most bank stock had low trade, including troubled Amman Investment Bank, which shed 0.20 dinars to 0.34 dinars.
Declining shares outnumbered gainers by 26 to fifteen, while 10 closed unchanged from Tuesday.
